title: Senses and the Nervous System
seo_title: Grade 6 Nervous System Worksheets: Stimulus, Receptors, Brain and Response
standard_text: Gather and synthesize information that sensory receptors respond to stimuli by sending messages to the brain for immediate behavior or storage as memories.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on the nervous system (NGSS MS-LS1-8): stimuli and sensory receptors, nerves, the brain and spinal cord, reflexes, memory and reaction-time data. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Receptors sense; the brain decides; muscles respond.
key_sub: Messages travel from receptors along nerves to the brain, which sends signals to the muscles or stores memories.
body_html:
How to think about it

The nervous system lets you sense and respond to the world.

Stimulus (light, sound, heat) → receptors (in eyes, ears, nose, tongue, skin) → sensory nerves → brain and spinal cord (process the information) → motor nerves → muscles (the response).

Some information is stored as memories that guide later behavior. A reflex, like pulling away from a hot stove, is very fast because the spinal cord responds before the brain thinks about it.

Example

You hear a car horn and step back. Stimulus? Response?

The horn is the stimulus.

Stepping back is the response.

Answer: horn; stepping back

Example

What decides how to respond?

Receptors detect; muscles act.

Answer: the brain

Common mistakes

  • Thinking receptors decide the response. The brain decides.
  • Mixing up the stimulus and the response.
  • Reversing the path: messages go from receptors to the brain, then to muscles.

faq.q: How does the nervous system work?
faq.a: Receptors detect a stimulus, sensory nerves carry the message to the brain, the brain processes it, and motor nerves tell the muscles how to respond.
A reflex is a fast, automatic response, like pulling your hand from a hot stove, that is handled by the spinal cord.
The brain stores information from past experiences, which helps us respond faster and better next time.
